newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes arbiter's ruling on Bosnian town.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes arbiter's ruling on Bosnian town.

text.p: The United States welcomed an arbitration ruling on Friday on the disputed Bosnian town of Brcko and called on rival factions to cooperate with the decision to put the town under international supervision.

U.S. arbiter Roberts Owen ruled that Brcko, claimed by both Serbs and Moslems, would be put under an international supervisor -- expected to be an American -- pending a final decision next year on its status.

"The United States welcomes the arbitral decision," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns. He called it a "fair decision" which "has the potential to make a substantial contribution to lasting peace in Bosnia."
"Under the terms of the Dayton agreement (on Bosnia), the parties are obligated to support and to implement the arbiter's decision," Burns told a news briefing.

"We call on all sides to exercise restraint and to work together to carry out this gradual and integrated programme of increased reconstruction assistance, the organised refugee return, and to provide for enhanced security in the Brcko area."

Brcko has key strategic importance in Bosnia, sitting astride a narrow land corridor linking the eastern and western halves of Serb territory. The Dayton accord divided Bosnia into a Serb Republic and a Moslem-Croat Federation.
Burns admitted that the failure to rule in favour of either party stemmed from lack of progress in implementing the Dayton accord in the Brcko area.
"The parties simply were not ready to accommodate a final decision by the tribunal as to the status of Brcko because of the continuing inter-ethnic problems and intolerance in the area," he said.
